findings.section: §3 (exclusion rules, three subtractions) vs the "What is NOT in scope" paragraph (lines 21-26)
findings.issue: The amendment asserts "No spent block — the ADORE t-F2F occurrence test or the prospective set — is re-scored, re-trained on or re-claimed", but §3 implements only three subtractions: the usable-acute filter, the six T2 classes, and the 11,437 prospective result_ids. The spent ADORE test result_ids are never subtracted, so rows from M4's already-scored primary test block land both in the new training pool (training on a spent test block) and inside T1_test (a second claim on rows already scored once). This breaks sota_campaign rule 1 and RESEARCH_PLAN §15.5 item 7, and it is the one subtraction the amendment names in prose and omits from the builder.
findings.evidence: Builder /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/sentinel_runs/chemtox/arch_v2/build_t1t6_split.py lines ~47-62 apply only T2_CLASSES and the prospective result_id set; no ADORE split file is read. Spent status: /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/SENTINEL-STOCKHOLM/results/registry.jsonl holds 63 rows with experiment=adore_chemtox_test, split=t-F2F/split_occurrence/test (notes: "single pre-registered test scoring (docs/preregistration/chemtox_test_plan.md)", n=4133). Overlap counted from /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/sentinel_data/processed/adore/split_assignments.parquet (assignment=='test') against the sealed split file: t-F2F/split_occurrence 4,133 test ids → 3,772 inside the universe, of which train_pool 2,859 and T1_test 913. Secondary spent endpoints scored in the same pass (chemtox_test_plan.md:19) add more: t-F2F/split_scaffold-murcko 4,238 (train_pool 3,117 / T1_test 1,121); t-C2C/split_occurrence 970 (784 / 186); a-CA2F-diff/split_occurrence 3,347 (2,756 / 591). T6a/T6b overlap is 0 (ADORE is in-window).
findings.suggested_ruling: Not stampable as written. A fourth subtraction must be added to the builder and to §3: every result_id with assignment=='test' in processed/adore/split_assignments.parquet for every ADORE challenge/split that carries a registry row under experiment adore_chemtox_test (t-F2F/split_occurrence, t-F2F/split_scaffold-murcko, t-C2C/split_occurrence, a-CA2F-diff/split_occurrence), with the removed count recorded; the split file, the cluster file and all §2 hashes are then rebuilt as _v2 and the MDEs recomputed before any stamp.

findings.section: §10.1 final paragraph (auxiliary rows) against §1/§2/§7.1 (T1 = held-out chemical clusters)
findings.issue: §10.1 states only that "The §3 subtractions apply to auxiliary rows too — no chronic or BCF row whose result_id is in the prospective frame, and no row from a T2-reserved class, enters any training set." The cluster hold-out is not applied to auxiliary rows. The reservation in §8 is by the result_ids of the three blocks, which does not reach the chronic (H3), censored-acute (H2) or BCF (H4) rows of the same chemicals. So ted/R3/mmoe may train on measured toxicity labels for the very chemicals that constitute T1_test, and T1's premise ("a chemical nobody has tested"; §1) and condition (g) parity are both compromised. The amendment's own §9 already shows the hole for H4 (588 H4 chemicals in the universe vs 456 in the pool).
findings.evidence: Amendment §10.1 lists only the two subtractions; no cluster filter appears for H2/H3/H4 anywhere in the file. Counted on CPU (2 threads) from /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/sentinel_data/processed/ecotox/ecotox_aquatic.parquet after the same T2-class and prospective subtractions, joined to the sealed split and docs/preregistration/chemtox_t1_clusters_v1.csv: held-out clusters 490 → 727 held-out CAS. H3 chronic (value+smiles+uncensored): 30,160 rows for 455 held-out CAS, of which 29,604 rows belong to CAS present in T1_test. H2 censored acute: 1,329 rows for held-out CAS, 1,292 of them T1_test CAS. H4: §9 / h4_bcf_join_qc.json overlap_with_tracks gives 588 shared with the universe vs 456 with the train pool, i.e. 132 BCF chemicals outside the pool.
findings.suggested_ruling: Not stampable as written. §10.1 must be amended, before the stamp, to state that no auxiliary row (H2, H3, H4, or any future auxiliary target) whose test_cas falls in a held-out t1_cluster enters any training set for any entry on any track, enforced as an assertion in the loader and reported as a count; otherwise T1 carries no §15.1 label.

findings.section: §3 ("One consequence stated plainly") and §7.1 (T6 folds) against §10.1 (auxiliary rows)
findings.issue: §3 and §7.1 rest T6's whole disclosure on "the pool is in-window only", so that selection extrapolates at most 2x. That is true only of the H1 acute pool. §10.1 admits H3 chronic and H2 censored rows to training with no duration filter, and chronic exposures are overwhelmingly outside 24-96 h. A model trained on them has seen labelled long- and short-duration data for the same chemistry as T6a, so the stated 2x selection limit, the "structural handicap" argument of §1 and the honesty of the §3 disclosure all fail, in the direction that favours the candidate over the tree comparators.
findings.evidence: Amendment §3 lines 136-139 and §7.1 lines 331-336 ("the selection range is at most 2x"); §10.1 imposes no duration condition on auxiliary rows. Counted from ecotox_aquatic.parquet after the same subtractions: 111,063 chronic rows (value+smiles+uncensored) lie outside 24-96 h, of which 84,812 belong to CAS present in train_pool. The sealed split file carries no auxiliary rows at all (columns: result_id, test_cas, t1_cluster, duration_h, block), so nothing frozen constrains them.
findings.suggested_ruling: Not stampable as written. Either (i) auxiliary rows are restricted to 24 <= duration_h <= 96 for every T6 entry, with the count of excluded rows recorded, or (ii) the §3 and §7.1 disclosures are rewritten to state the true maximum labelled duration seen in training, and T6's "structurally handicapped comparator" argument is withdrawn. Option (i) is the conservative choice and the lead should require it.

findings.section: §3 partition table (SD(target), Replicate floor columns) and §6 ("From counts and metadata only")
findings.issue: §6 asserts the design numbers came "From counts and metadata only" and that "no label of any future test row informed any number in this table". The MDE table itself is label-invariant, but §3's table publishes SD(target) and a pooled within-group replicate floor for T1_test, T6a_test and T6b_test — six statistics computed directly from the protected label column of the three sealed blocks — and §6 then uses the per-block floor as a binding absolute bound. Lead rule 2 permits "labels of protected rows: counts only". §13's forbidden list is written as "any read of T1_test, T6a_test or T6b_test beyond the row counts in §3", which exempts the read that had already occurred. The read cannot be undone by a ruling; the file must not be stamped while it presents these as counts-only.
findings.evidence: build_t1t6_split.py block_stats() computes sd_target from df["log10_conc_mol_L"] for every block, and the following loop computes replicate_floor per test block from the same column; t1t6_counts.json records sd_target 1.7415 / 1.6806 / 1.7678 and replicate_floor 0.4954 / 0.4083 / 0.4578 for T1_test / T6a_test / T6b_test. unseen_taxa.mde (sentinel/models/chemtox/unseen_taxa.py:665-669) reads TARGET and returns sd_target, which t1t6_mde.json records per case; the script's 1e-12 assertion covers only mde_log_units and mde_log_units_rho0 (compute_t1t6_mde.py), not sd_target. LEAD_DECISIONS_20261110.md rule 2: "build data (labels of protected rows: counts only)".
findings.suggested_ruling: Before any stamp the author strikes the SD(target) and Replicate floor entries for the three test blocks from §3 and from the §6 text, keeping only the train_pool floor (0.504) as the absolute bound, and adds a dated disclosure that these six aggregates were computed on 2026-11-10 before the blocks were reserved. The lead records the read in the rulings file; it does not spend a look, but it is not re-characterised as counts-only.

findings.section: §2 frozen-artefact table, rows "Row partition, label-free" and "Builder (deterministic; reproduces both files)"
findings.issue: The builder does not produce the sealed split file. It writes an eight-column parquet that includes the target column, to a session scratchpad, with a different hash. That file still exists: 1,609,554 B, mode -rw-rw-r--, mtime 2026-11-10 12:25. The cluster CSV does reproduce (cluster_file_sha256 == a6e33634..., matches §2 and the on-disk 0444 file). All eight §2 hashes verified equal.
findings.suggested_ruling: Binding: the builder is extended so it writes the label-free five-column split file itself and the column drop is in-script; §2's "reproduces both files" is corrected or the exact derivation command is recorded in the rulings file; and the label-bearing scratchpad partition is deleted or moved under seal_dir (0444 + SHA256SUMS) with its hash recorded, before the stamp.

findings.section: §6 ("Computed by sentinel.models.chemtox.unseen_taxa.mde — the project's own pinned helper, the same function that produced T2's 0.011 / 0.019 / 0.021")
findings.issue: The helper restricts itself to the ADORE applicability domain. The arch-v2 script sets that flag to True for every row, so the restriction is bypassed and the MDE is computed over all rows. The helper is indeed the pinned module, but it is invoked on a wider basis than T2 used, which makes the MDEs smaller (tighter), makes §6's direct comparison with T2's 0.011 / 0.019 / 0.021 not like-for-like, and lowers the §12.1(f) claim threshold. The amendment never mentions the flag.
findings.evidence: sentinel/models/chemtox/unseen_taxa.py:109 sets in_adore_domain = chem_structure_class.isin(ADORE_STRUCTURE_CLASSES); line 664 inside mde() does dom = block[block["in_adore_domain"]]. compute_t1t6_mde.py line 23: part["in_adore_domain"] = True. The pin is intact — sha256 of unseen_taxa.py is cf1493c60f694741528a3ef751fb467d89e5ff9428ee42788ed32f6c4f00a4de, equal to module_sha256 in docs/preregistration/chemtox_unseen_taxa_pins.json (guard and plan hashes also match).
findings.suggested_ruling: Binding: §6 must disclose that in_adore_domain is forced True so no applicability-domain restriction is applied, state that the T2 figures were computed on the restricted subset and are therefore not directly comparable, and either report the domain-restricted MDE alongside or declare the unrestricted value as the single binding threshold. The stricter of the two values governs condition (f).

findings.section: §6, closing sentence after the MDE table ("Every block is better powered than T2's best (0.011)")
findings.issue: False for T6b. Its primary MDE at rho=0.9 is 0.0197, almost twice T2's best of 0.011, i.e. T6b is the worst-powered block of any quoted here. The sentence is a power claim that sits directly above kill rule 8, which already concedes T6b may be underpowered in practice, so the file contradicts itself in the direction that flatters the weakest block.
findings.evidence: Amendment §6 table: T6b_test primary MDE (rho=0.9) 0.0197, confirmed in /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/sentinel_runs/chemtox/arch_v2/t1t6_mde.json. Same §6 paragraph claims every block beats 0.011; §12.2 rule 8 refers to "its 0.0197 MDE". Lower MDE = better powered.
findings.suggested_ruling: Binding correction: the sentence is restricted to T1_test and T6a_test; T6b is recorded as worse powered than T2's best block and its 0.0197 threshold is restated as the binding bar for any T6b claim.

findings.issue: Condition (a) requires a paired CI, resampled on the block's own unit, against the strongest published method on that block. R5 supplies TRIDENT's per-SMILES errors from the authors' own 10x10 CV on their own split, not errors on T1_test/T6 rows, so no paired per-row difference on our blocks can be formed from it, and the amendment itself says TRIDENT's training data overlaps our rows. RESEARCH_PLAN §15.1 requires the strongest published method to be "re-run on our split when code exists"; §10.2 records that TRIDENT's source and weights do exist and are deliberately not downloaded. If R5 wins the pre-look "strongest published" selection of §4.3, condition (a) becomes unsatisfiable, and kill rule 3 only covers the case where the released file lacks usable errors.
findings.evidence: Amendment §4.2 R5 ("head-to-head via its released per-SMILES 10x10-CV errors, never by re-running TRIDENT"); §12.1(a) ("paired CI (cluster bootstrap, 2,000 resamples, unit = the block's resampling unit) excluding 0 against the strongest published method on that block"); §10.2 ("the 2.8 GB weights and 3.2 GB source archives are not downloaded"); RESEARCH_PLAN.md §15.1 line ~361: "(re-run on our split when code exists, or on the published benchmark split)". docs/licenses.md:47 confirms CC BY 4.0 and the two file sizes, so the licence is not the obstacle.
findings.suggested_ruling: Binding: R5 is descriptive and contextual only and can never satisfy condition (a). Condition (a) on every block is read against the strongest published comparator actually re-run on our rows at parity (mmoe, gpboost_published, or a TRIDENT re-train from source with our rows excluded), chosen on pool validation before the look, and the inability to pair against TRIDENT's published errors is disclosed beside every claim.

Separately, the lead's cap wording is "T1 384 searched configurations, T6 128, plus fixed baselines"; the 12 ablations are neither searched nor baselines, so their place relative to the cap is undeclared.

LEAD_DECISIONS_20261110.md M4 update: "Caps as in plan §8.2: T1 384 searched configurations, T6 128, plus fixed baselines; every configuration counted"; M4_architecture_plan.md §8.2 states the same.

The registry carries the corrected per-track totals.

findings.section: §5.7 ("Budget 22-30 GPU-h for ted, <= 1 GPU-h for timehead, 8-12 GPU-h for mmoe, 1-2 GPU-h for the embedding cache")
findings.issue: The GPU-hour figures are carried over from the plan unchanged while the number of fits they must cover has roughly quadrupled, and one GPU entry has no budget at all. ted is now 32 configurations x 4 folds on T1 plus 16 x 3 on T6 = 176 fits against the plan's 48-job basis for the same 22-30 GPU-h; mmoe is likewise 176 fits against 8-12 GPU-h (about 4 minutes per fit). rx_chemprop is a GPU entry with 32 configurations x 4 folds = 128 fits and appears in no budget line. An unachievable budget is the kind of thing that gets renegotiated mid-campaign once partial results exist, which is exactly what §5.6 and kill rule 1 are meant to prevent.
findings.evidence: Amendment §5.1 entry 1 ted (GPU), entry 5 rx_chemprop ("chemprop D-MPNN single-task + embedding. GPU"), entry 6 mmoe; §7.1 T1 4 folds, T6 3 folds; §5.3 T6 16 configurations per entry; §5.7 budget list omits rx_chemprop. M4_architecture_plan.md §8.2 phase P5: "16 configurations x 3 folds = 48 jobs ... 22-30 GPU-h, cap 32". 176 fits at the amendment's own 30 min/job fallback trigger is about 88 GPU-h.
findings.suggested_ruling: Binding: §5.7 is replaced before the stamp by a per-entry fit count and a per-entry GPU-hour ceiling that includes rx_chemprop, with a total ceiling; if the ceiling is reached, the pre-declared fallback to 8 configurations per track applies automatically and is recorded, and no budget is renegotiated after any validation number exists.

findings.section: §8 ("Reserved from today, and never used for training or tuning by any workstream")
findings.issue: The amendment reserves the three blocks only inside itself. The project-wide list that other workstreams read, sota_campaign.md's "Reserved unseen blocks" sections, does not mention them, and the amendment states it edits no other file. M2's Test-S, M5-F, M1-SP and M7 P2 were all recorded there by the lead, so M4's new blocks are the only arch-v2 reservation invisible outside its own workstream, while "never used by ANY workstream" is a project-wide obligation over a shared ECOTOX frame.

LEAD_DECISIONS_20261110.md records the same pattern for M2 ("Test-S is reserved from now (see sota_campaign.md)") and M5-F.
findings.suggested_ruling: Binding, executed by the lead at the stamp: an entry is added to sota_campaign.md's "Reserved unseen blocks added 2026-11-10" section naming the T1_test, T6a_test and T6b_test rows of chemtox_t1t6_split_v1.parquet (sha256 005f7957...), reserved from 2026-11-10, with the row counts 10,548 / 13,059 / 2,410 and the instruction that any workstream touching ECOTOX excludes these result_ids and reports overlap as counts.

findings.section: §1 ("or by the M5 BioAssess freeze (chemtox/{__init__,evaluate,features,tabpfn_model}.py, gpboost_model.py)") and §11 ("that file is covered by an existing freeze and is not edited")
findings.issue: gpboost_model.py is not frozen by either test the project uses: it is not mode 0444 and it appears in no freeze-candidate hash list. The four files named alongside it are 0444. The amendment uses the unsupported freeze claim as its reason for leaving a known incorrect L6 article title in live code, and other agents are editing this repo now, so nothing actually protects either the file or the correction.
findings.evidence: ls -la /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/SENTINEL-STOCKHOLM/sentinel/models/chemtox/: __init__.py, evaluate.py, features.py, tabpfn_model.py are -r--r--r--; gpboost_model.py is -rw-rw-r-- (5,392 B, 2026-10-24 22:13). docs/preregistration/bioassess_x_freeze_candidate.json contains no "gpboost_model" string; no SHA256SUMS under any chemtox path lists it. The defect itself is real: gpboost_model.py:11 reads "...Unlocking a generic modeling approach for species sensitivity predictions" while M4_architecture_plan.md:202 gives the verified L6 title "...Unlocking a new level of predictive power for machine learning-based ecotoxicity predictions by exploiting chemical and biological information". chemtox_unseen_taxa_plan.md:905-909 made the same unsupported freeze claim.

Either the lead names the freeze and hash list that covers it, or the one-line citation is corrected under the lead's own change control and the file is then sealed 0444 with its hash recorded in the rulings file. findings.section: §3 (out-of-window definition, "5,486 below 24 h") and §4.3 T6-only crude-rule baselines (Haber's rule)
findings.issue: No plausibility floor is declared for duration_h, although §9 declares one for BCF. The T6 blocks contain rows at exactly 0 h, which is not a physical exposure, and 424 rows below 1 h. Haber's rule (C x t constant) is the regulatory baseline T6 is motivated against and is undefined at t = 0, so the designated crude-rule floor cannot be evaluated on part of its own block, and an implementation choice made at scoring time would be a post-hoc decision inside the single look.
findings.evidence: Counted from the sealed split file (counts only): duration_h == 0 in 3 rows (T6a_test 2, T6b_test 1); duration_h < 1 in 424 rows; duration_h < 24 by block T6a_test 4,522 / T6b_test 964 (sum 5,486, matching §3). t1t6_counts.json records duration_min 0.0 for both T6a_test and T6b_test. build_t1t6_split.py applies no lower bound on duration_h, only notna(). Amendment §4.3 names "Haber's rule (C x t constant)" as a T6-only baseline; §9 by contrast declares an explicit trim log10 BCF in [-2, 7].
findings.suggested_ruling: Binding, declared before the stamp: a minimum plausible duration is fixed now (e.g. duration_h >= 0.25), rows below it are dropped from all four blocks with the count recorded and the §2 hashes rebuilt; or, if no row is dropped, the Haber's-rule baseline's behaviour at t -> 0 is specified here in closed form. The choice is made before any look, not at scoring time.

findings.section: §4.2 reference R4 against §4.3 (ADORE published RF / XGBoost; GPBoost published) and the enumerations in §5.2 / §5.4
findings.issue: R4 says "Every comparator gets the concatenated embedding block ... parity requires it for R1-R3, rf, xgboost and the published configurations". §4.3 says the published ADORE and GPBoost arms use "verbatim published configurations" and "hyper-parameters verbatim from the authors' released models". A verbatim published configuration fed a concatenated foundation-model embedding is no longer verbatim, and the §5.2/§5.4 enumerations list each published entry exactly once, so the counted design follows §4.3 and not R4. Since §12.1(g) turns on which comparators "received the same inputs", the ambiguity decides after the fact which arms count as parity-matched.
findings.evidence: Amendment §4.2 row R4; §4.3 bullets 1 and 3; §5.2 lists rf_published_adore 1, xgboost_published_adore 1, gpboost_published 2 with no embedding-fed twin; §5.4 the same minus the trivial per-species/per-chemical arms. T6's §5.3/§5.4 also contain no rf arm with the embedding, so R4's "rf" clause has no T6 entry at all.
findings.suggested_ruling: Binding: §4.3 governs for the published arms, which stay verbatim and without the embedding and are reported as published-form comparators only; R4 parity applies to R1-R3 and to the re-tuned rf/xgboost arms, which are the arms condition (g) is read against. If the lead instead wants embedding-fed published twins, they must be enumerated as extra configurations inside the caps before the stamp.

findings.section: §3 ("T6's test blocks reach 274x beyond 96 h") and §6/§7.1 repeats
findings.issue: The 274x figure is T6a's alone. T6b's longest exposure is 8,035.5 h, about 84x beyond 96 h. Writing it as a property of "T6's test blocks" overstates the stricter block's reach, which matters because §12.2 rule 8 fixes T6b as a full block with its own look.
findings.evidence: t1t6_counts.json blocks: T6a_test duration_max 26298.0 (26298/96 = 273.9); T6b_test duration_max 8035.5 (8035.5/96 = 83.7). Amendment §3 and §7.1 attribute 274x to "T6's test blocks" without distinguishing them.
findings.suggested_ruling: Record only: the write-up states the extrapolation reach per block, 274x for T6a and 84x for T6b. No action before the stamp.

points.point: The disclosed T6 extrapolation asymmetry: the training pool is in-window only, so T6 selection can extrapolate at most 2x while the test blocks reach 274x; the alternative of putting part of the long tail into the pool was rejected (§3, §7.1).
points.recommendation: Accept the design, but only after C3 is fixed, and bind two conditions. First, the claim that selection reaches at most 2x must be made true: restrict every auxiliary row (H2, H3) fed to any T6 entry to 24-96 h, or restate the real maximum labelled duration seen in training and drop the "structurally handicapped comparator" argument. Second, since selection provably cannot verify long-range shape, require the T6 look to report the primary metric stratified by the pre-declared duration bands, with the >2160 h band named in advance as the band the claim rests on, so a win concentrated in the 96-168 h band cannot be presented as duration extrapolation. The rejection of the long-tail-in-pool alternative is itself correct and should be upheld.
points.reason: The author's reasoning (putting the tail in the pool shrinks the regime under test) is sound and conservative. The flaw is not the choice but the disclosure: as written the "in-window only" premise is contradicted by §10.1's unfiltered auxiliary rows, and a selection-to-test gap of 2x versus 274x means the single look is the only evidence for the shape claim, so its reporting granularity must be fixed before results exist rather than chosen afterwards.

points.point: The 544-configuration total against the lead's caps (T1 384 searched, T6 128 searched, plus fixed baselines).
points.recommendation: Do not accept 544 as declared. Require the corrected arithmetic (T1 401, T6 143, grand total 544 across 38 entries) and a sentence placing the 12 ablation fits outside the 384/128 searched caps as fixed fits of the single selected ted configuration, not as search budget. Hold the searched caps at exactly 384 and 128: no entry may exceed 32 (T1) or 16 (T6) configurations, no family may be re-screened, and a failed fit still consumes its slot. Pair this with C10: the realised GPU budget must be declared per entry, because an unachievable budget is the most likely route to a mid-campaign cap renegotiation.
points.reason: The searched counts and the entry enumerations are correct and within the lead's caps, and the ablations are separately approved by the lead's "TED (with ablations A1-A6)", so the substance is compliant. But 395 + 137 = 532 while the declared grand total is 544, and §5.6 wires those same figures into the registry as the drift check, so the reconciliation the amendment relies on would fail against itself. Fixing the arithmetic before the stamp costs nothing; fixing it after a result exists looks like adjusting the denominator.

points.point: Track T5 (cross-source transfer) blocked on the EnviroTox licence.
points.recommendation: Uphold the block and keep it recorded as blocked rather than skipped, exactly as the amendment has it.
